revision: Workbench HEAD 0534135d877ec3679bb91ee0b4a68b71e174ff7a plus the dirty WB-01..WB-20 tree and tested WB-21 changes. No commit or push was made.
environment: macOS 26.4.1 arm64, Macmini9,1; Neovim 0.11.7 minimum and 0.12.4 current/host; Python 3.14.6; mini.test 0.16.0; pynvim 0.6.0; msgpack 1.1.1. Linux was unavailable locally.
summary: Implemented a bounded, reviewed local-filesystem operation service for exclusive file/directory creation, regular-file copy, rename/move, and adapter-backed recoverable trash. Paths and source/target/parent preimages are revalidated before mutation; case-only rename uses an intermediate hard link, copy verifies bytes/mode/identity, open clean buffers are rebound with text/undo retained, and dirty/symlink/outside-root/cyclic/cross-device/overwrite cases fail closed. Workspace rename requests honor static/dynamic LSP filters and encoding, apply a compatible bounded WorkspaceEdit before filesystem rename, and send didRenameFiles only after success. Resource operations and malformed/oversized edits are refused. Active plans are capped at 32, terminal payloads are released, and only 32 terminal summaries are retained. Directories are not moved/renamed/copied; default trash and permanent deletion are unavailable; cross-device moves are unsupported.

gates.command: make check-ownership; review docs/tasks.json#WB-21 ownership and claimed paths
gates.result: Ownership validation passed for 36 Workbench Lua modules. WB-21 changes are within the claimed operations service, LSP/files providers, Files controller, tests, Makefile and docs/evidence paths. No sibling plugin, root config, Nix input, host default, or external repository was changed by this task.

All 146 mini.test cases passed on Neovim 0.11.7 and 0.12.4. WB-21 service tests cover create/collision/overlap, byte-verified copy and permission preservation, move/rename/case-only rename, buffer undo/rebind, stale and dirty preimages, hard-link collisions, symlinks/outside-root/cyclic moves, injected permissions/EXDEV/partial writes, trash adapters, LSP ordering/recovery, bounded plans and disposal. Provider/controller tests cover filters, encoding, conflicts, malformed/resource edits, cancellation, exact review, trash hiding and stale confirmation suppression.

gates.command: make test; inspect cancellation, stale-generation, overlap, failure-recovery and disposal tests
gates.result: Cancelling/disposal of in-flight file-operation requests cancels native LSP requests and ignores late replies. A Files workspace/root change cancels a pending review and its late confirmation cannot mutate the old workspace. Overlapping plans are rejected, stale preimages fail before mutation, partial copy cleans only its owned inode, uncertain LSP application records manual recovery and suppresses didRenameFiles, and service/controller/provider/layout resource inventories are empty after disposal. Active plans are bounded at 32.

The actual RPC/ext_linegrid flow passed on both Neovim versions at all four grid sizes. It opens Files from an editor-owned origin, types a real filename, renders the exact operation/path before mutation, confirms the explicit Apply item, observes the empty created file and refreshed tree, then closes Files and verifies editor cwd/buffer/focus preservation and zero active requests/resources after disposal. The destination remained absent until confirmation.

gates.command: make test; inspect WB-21 injected stale/collision/permission/symlink/cross-device/partial-copy/LSP failure tests and real review grids
gates.result: Failure evidence proves no silent overwrite for existing files or hard links; stale source/workspace generation, dirty buffers, symlinks, outside-root targets, directory cycles, permissions, cross-device links, conflicting/malformed/oversized LSP edits and unsupported LSP resource operations fail closed. Partial copy cleanup checks inode ownership; uncertain WorkspaceEdit application is recorded as manual recovery and no didRenameFiles success notification is sent. Case-only rename preserves the exact directory entry; clean open-buffer rename preserves text and undo. Default trash is unavailable and hidden without an adapter; the injected adapter must provide a recoverable receipt. No permanent-delete action is exposed.
